# Project structure

The previous section is "where Python looks". This section is "what it looks *for*, and how we put *our* code on that path".

## Module vs package

A **module** is one importable file. `math_utils.py` is the module `math_utils`:

```python
# math_utils.py
def quat_mul(a, b):
    ...
```

```python
import math_utils
math_utils.quat_mul(q1, q2)
```

A **package** is a directory of modules. The directory name is the import prefix. We always include `__init__.py` so the intent is obvious ([PEP 420](https://peps.python.org/pep-0420/) also allows *namespace packages* without it; we do not rely on that):

```text
robotics/
  __init__.py           # may be empty, or re-export public names
  math_utils.py
  ik/
    __init__.py
    differential.py
```

```python
from robotics.math_utils import quat_mul
from robotics.ik.differential import damped_lstsq
```

`robotics.ik` is a **subpackage**: a package nested in another. The dotted name is just the folder path with `/` replaced by `.`.

`__init__.py` can re-export so callers do not have to know the internal layout:

```python
# robotics/__init__.py
from robotics.math_utils import quat_mul
```

```python
from robotics import quat_mul   # instead of robotics.math_utils
```

Keep that thin. A huge `__init__.py` that imports everything makes every `import robotics` slow and creates circular-import traps. Worse: module-level training, file I/O, or env mutation in imported files — see [Things not to do — import-time side effects](things-not-to-do.qmd#import-time-side-effects).

## What Python actually searches for

For `import robotics`, Python still walks `sys.path`. At each directory it tries, in order:

- `robotics.py` (a module), then
- `robotics/` (a package)

The **first match wins**. That is why "it works in the notebook but not as a script" is common: you started the notebook from a different working directory, so a different folder sat at `sys.path[0]`.

Relative imports (`from .math_utils import quat_mul`) only work *inside* a package, and only when that package was imported as a package — not when you run the file as a script (`python robotics/math_utils.py`). Run scripts as scripts; import library code as a package.

## Making our code importable

This folder *is* the example project:

```text
onboarding/
  pyproject.toml
  src/
    robotics/              # this is what you import
      __init__.py
      math_utils.py
      ik/
        __init__.py
        differential.py
  scripts/
    helpers.py             # neighbor of train.py — not a package
    train.py               # you run this; you do not import it
```

Three patterns, from "fine for a one-off" to "how we actually work".

**1. Same folder (scripts talking to neighbors)**

`scripts/train.py` can do `from helpers import greet` because running `python scripts/train.py` puts `scripts/` on `sys.path[0]`. Fine for a tiny helper that only that script needs. Breaks as soon as two scripts in different folders both want `helpers`, or you want `from robotics.ik import …` from a notebook started elsewhere.

**2. [`PYTHONPATH`](environment-variables.qmd#pythonpath) (temporary; do not rely on this in a team)**

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/train.py
```

Puts `src/` on `sys.path`. Convenient for an afternoon, fragile: everyone must remember the same [environment variable](environment-variables.qmd#pythonpath), and IDEs / debuggers will not. Same class of problem as `sys.path.insert` in code — see [Things not to do — hacking `sys.path`](things-not-to-do.qmd#hacking-sys.path).

**3. Install the package into the environment (what we actually do)**

[`pyproject.toml`](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/) tells the installer the package name, its dependencies, and that importable code lives under `src/`. Then:

```bash
uv sync                 # or: pip install -e .
uv run python scripts/train.py
```

## Why `pip install -e .`

The `src/` layout is a firewall. `robotics/` is **not** a child of the directory you run from — it sits one level down, under `src/`. Python never searches inside `src/` on its own.

Walk through `python scripts/train.py` *before* installing:

1. Python puts `…/onboarding/scripts` on `sys.path[0]`.
2. It looks there for `robotics.py` or `robotics/` — not present (`helpers.py` is, which is why `import helpers` still works).
3. It looks in the env's `site-packages` — `robotics` is not there either.
4. `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'robotics'`.

The same failure happens from a REPL or notebook unless the working directory happens to be `src/` (do not depend on that).

`pip install -e .` does two jobs:

1. **Install dependencies** listed in `pyproject.toml` into the environment (here, NumPy) — the same mechanism as `pip install numpy`.
2. **Register our package** in that environment's `site-packages`, so `import robotics` uses the same lookup as `import numpy`.

The **`-e` is the part that matters while you are writing code**. It means *editable* (also called a develop install).

| Command | What lands in `site-packages` | Edit `src/robotics/math_utils.py` |
|---|---|---|
| `pip install .` | A **copy** of the package | Python still imports the stale copy until you reinstall |
| `pip install -e .` | A **link** (`.pth` / egg-link) pointing at `src/` | Next `import` sees your live files |

Research is edit-run-edit. A copied install would force a reinstall after every change. Editable installs are [PEP 660](https://peps.python.org/pep-0660/) / `pip install -e` — the only mode that is usable day to day.

`uv sync` does this editable install of the current project automatically. `uv pip install -e .` and `pip install -e .` are the explicit form — same effect. You only need to re-run the install when **metadata** changes (new dependency, renamed package), not when you edit `.py` files.

After it works, check that you got *your* tree, not a copy:

```bash
uv run python -c "import robotics; print(robotics.__file__)"
# …/onboarding/src/robotics/__init__.py
```

Then check that it does **not** depend on the current working directory:

```bash
cd /tmp
uv run --directory /path/to/onboarding python -c "import robotics; print(robotics.__file__)"
```

If that still prints a path under `src/`, the package lives on the environment — which is the whole point.

## `src/` layout

Importable packages live under `src/`; scripts you *run* live under `scripts/`. Installing via `pyproject.toml` is what makes `from robotics.ik.differential import damped_lstsq` work from `scripts/train.py`, a notebook, or a test. See [PyPA src layout](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/) and [References](references.qmd#packaging-and-environments).

Do not give a script the same name as a package you need (`robotics.py` next to the `robotics/` package). First match on `sys.path` wins.

## Case studies: two repos to read

This onboarding repo is intentionally tiny. To see the same ideas at real scale, skim **two**
 public trees — one **basic** (single library you could fork tomorrow), one **advanced**
 (research codebase with experiments, extras, and CI). You are learning **layout**, not
 cloning every file.

### How to read any repo (10 minutes)

1. Open **`pyproject.toml`** (or legacy `setup.cfg` / `setup.py`) — package name, dependencies, optional extras, where code lives.
2. Find **importable code** — usually `src/<package>/` ([src layout](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/)).
3. Find **runnable entrypoints** — `scripts/`, `examples/`, `benchmarks/`, or console scripts declared in `pyproject.toml`. These are what you *run*; they should import the library, not be imported themselves.
4. Glance at **`tests/`** — how they import the package (editable install in CI?).
5. Ignore noise on first pass: `.github/`, Docker, pre-commit — note they exist, copy patterns later.

### Basic — [hynek/structlog](https://github.com/hynek/structlog)

A single-purpose library: structured logging. The tree is close to **our** layout, with
 grown-up packaging.

| Path | Lesson |
|---|---|
| `src/structlog/` | One importable package; submodules by topic (`_config.py`, processors, …) |
| `pyproject.toml` | `[project]`, dependencies, `[tool.*]` for ruff/mypy/pytest |
| `tests/` | Mirrors package layout; shows `pip install -e .` / `pytest` workflow |
| `docs/` | Sphinx site — separate from importable code |
| `show_off.py` | Small runnable demo at repo root (like our `scripts/`, but minimal) |

**Study questions:** Where would you add a new public function? How does `tests/` import
 `structlog` without `sys.path` hacks? What is *not* shipped to PyPI (docs, bench, tox)?

Good **first clone** when you want “one package, done right” without robot hardware.

### Advanced — [huggingface/lerobot](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot)

A robot-learning stack: datasets, policies, hardware drivers, training scripts. Same
 **src/** discipline, but many moving parts.

| Path | Lesson |
|---|---|
| `src/lerobot/` | Library code split into subpackages (`common`, `datasets`, `policies`, …) |
| `examples/` | Runnable training / eval scripts — import `lerobot`, not the other way around |
| `tests/` | Broad coverage; CI runs against editable install |
| `pyproject.toml` | Core deps vs **`[project.optional-dependencies]`** (hardware, sim, dev) |
| `.github/workflows/` | How the maintainers enforce lint/test on every PR |

**Study questions:** What lives in the library vs `examples/`? Which extras would you
 `uv sync --extra …` for sim-only vs real hardware? Where would a one-off ablation script
 go so it does not become import-time baggage?

Good **second clone** when your thesis repo needs scripts *and* a reusable package —
 typical in imitation learning and RL.

### Basic vs advanced (at a glance)

| | **structlog** (basic) | **LeRobot** (advanced) |
|---|---|---|
| Goal | Small library on PyPI | Research + hardware + training |
| Importable code | `src/structlog/` | `src/lerobot/` + many subpackages |
| Runnable work | `show_off.py`, docs examples | `examples/`, CLI entrypoints |
| Optional deps | Few | Many (`[project.optional-dependencies]`) |
| What to copy first | `src/` + `pyproject.toml` + `tests/` | Splitting library vs experiments, extras groups |

Neither repo is a template to copy wholesale into a paper-sized project — borrow **structure**,
 not every workflow file. When in doubt, stay closer to **structlog** until you outgrow it.

## A mental model

| You want to… | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Use `numpy`, `torch`, … | Installed into the env's `site-packages` |
| Use *our* library from anywhere in that env | `pyproject.toml` + `uv sync` / `uv pip install -e .` — not `sys.path` hacks ([Things not to do](things-not-to-do.qmd#hacking-sys.path)) |
| Run a one-off script that imports a neighbor file | Script directory on `sys.path` (ok for small tutorials) |
| Load a data file or asset from disk reliably | Anchor with `pathlib.Path(__file__)` — see [Things not to do — paths](things-not-to-do.qmd#hard-coded-absolute-paths-and-naive-relative-paths) |
| Debug `ModuleNotFoundError` | `sys.executable` (wrong env), then `sys.path` (never installed / shadowed) |
